target_name: Restated Cash Yield in Rollover-Safe Innovators
rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals (gen-8 pre-innovation cash-earnings yield + knowledge share, and gen-8 hard-book with the che>dlc rollover state) with no new construct, and since both legs are already measured the outcome is a predictable interpolation rather than a test of a new mechanism.

target_name: Fully Restated Intangible Cash Yield and Share
rationale: The internal-consistency argument — the same organic intangible spend defined in both the flow numerator and the capital-share conditioner — is the one genuinely principled construction in this batch, though be aware that xad is missing for most firms (COALESCE to zero) and that both legs load positively on xrd, pushing the composite toward the known R&D-to-market anomaly rather than a distinct effect.

target_name: Stock and Flow Cheapness Both Restated
rationale: Averaging two anchors that share the same market-cap denominator and have each already been tested with the identical conditioner will almost certainly land between their known results (alpha 6.1%/fmb 4.4 and alpha 4.4%/fmb 7.7), so this is a cosmetic blend rather than a test of the claimed fmb-alpha "frontier."

target_name: Cheap Firms with Research-Induced Negative Cash Earnings
rationale: The state is the same mechanism as the archive's gen-5 "Cheap Firms Whose Losses Are R&D-Induced" with the profitability line swapped from ib to ebitda, which is close to a cosmetic variant, and the narrower EBITDA-negative-but-EBITDA+R&D-positive condition will concentrate the long leg in tiny pre-revenue biotech names, raising instability rather than sharpening the mechanism — the expression itself is internally consistent with the hypothesis.

target_name: Restated Cash Yield with Unmonetized Pipeline
rationale: Coherent and correctly signed, but it is another cell in an already-mapped 2x2 of archive anchors and conditioners (pre-innovation yield × pipeline/revenue), and the "both are income-statement quantities" rationale is a presentational point rather than an economic reason to expect a different result.

All three legs — hard-book cheapness, the brand-inclusive organic share, and the che>dlc indicator — are already individually evaluated in the archive, and the stated motivation is inconsistent with the construction since a soft SUMRANK tilt does not "exclude" term-financed firms, so nothing about the long-term-debt-aversion diagnosis is actually being tested.
